summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of AlgoMásQueLuz OS. 25/26 backend tests passed; frontend login + nav + all critical pages render correctly with backend integration working.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout never triggers in production. Identifier is `{request.client.host}:{email}` but behind the Kubernetes ingress, `request.client.host` rotates between proxy IPs (observed 10.208.130.77 and 10.208.130.78 alternating), so each attempt creates/looks up a different login_attempts record. After 7 consecutive wrong attempts the API still returns 401, never 429. FIX: either (a) trust X-Forwarded-For (use ProxyHeadersMiddleware / forwarded_allow_ips='*') and parse the original client IP, or (b) use only email (or email + hashed IP from XFF) as the lockout identifier.

issues: Console warnings 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' from Recharts ResponsiveContainer — chart still renders fine but the parent container reports negative dimensions on initial mount. Non-blocking; consider setting minWidth/minHeight or fixed aspect ratio on the chart wrapper.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout to work behind proxy: trust X-Forwarded-For or change identifier to email-only (or email+XFF-IP). Currently the 5-attempts/15-min lockout is effectively disabled in production preview URL.
(Optional) Fix Recharts ResponsiveContainer width(-1) warning on Dashboard.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 944 lines — consider splitting into auth.py, clients.py, contracts.py, dashboard.py, documents.py, notifications.py modules for maintainability.

Brute-force protection uses request.client.host which is the immediate upstream proxy in Kubernetes — does not capture real client IP. Use Starlette's ProxyHeadersMiddleware or read X-Forwarded-For explicitly.
/api/clients DELETE allows gestor (via require_role('admin','gestor')) but no audit trail of who deleted what; consider soft-delete or audit log for B2B CRM.

Comercial users can list/patch/delete contracts for ANY client (no comercial-scoping in /api/contracts GET/PATCH/DELETE) — leaks data across comerciales. Only /api/clients enforces comercial isolation.
/api/documents GET and POST upload have no comercial scoping either; any authenticated user can list/upload to any client.

OCR endpoint stores the uploaded file under backend/uploads/{uuid}{ext} but there is no static file serving / downloads endpoint, so once uploaded, the actual file cannot be retrieved by the frontend.

Login response leaks access_token in body in addition to setting httpOnly cookie — defeats the purpose of httpOnly cookie strategy. Either remove the token from body or document that body token is intentional for non-browser clients.
No rate-limiting on /api/documents/upload — Gemini call is 10-30s and could be abused.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_backend.py covers auth (login/me/logout/brute-force/register-RBAC), clients (CRUD/search/filter/comercial-isolation), contracts (CRUD/sort), dashboard (stats/alerts), renovations, users, meta and OCR upload (non-blocking). OCR endpoint accepted the tiny PNG and returned ocr_status in valid set; the actual Gemini-3-Pro call result was not validated for correctness.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout fails because FastAPI's `request.client.host` reflects the direct TCP peer (the K8s ingress proxy) and the ingress load-balances across multiple proxy pods (observed alternating 10.208.130.77 / 10.208.130.78 in supervisor logs). Each request thus produces a different identifier `{ip}:{email}`, splitting the 5-attempt counter across rows. Repro: 7 consecutive POSTs to /api/auth/login with same wrong email from same client all return 401. Mitigation: add `app.add_middleware(ProxyHeadersMiddleware, trusted_hosts='*')` or read `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip()` for the identifier; alternatively, drop IP from the key and lock per email only (with a small CAPTCHA later).
